alternatives.root_cause: A wrong artifact was deployed to fraud-detection and cannot complete startup.
alternatives.why_not: The change log records only resource_limits edits, no image or version change, and the loop begins after a limit lowering.

alternatives.root_cause: A configuration value on fraud-detection is itself wrong, breaking startup.
alternatives.why_not: The only configuration touched is a memory ceiling; the failure is the process exceeding that ceiling at runtime, not a value naming something wrong.

alternatives.root_cause: flagd became slow or unreachable and fraud-detection failed waiting on it.
alternatives.why_not: No flagd changes and no flagd logs at all, and fraud-detection's traces show no slow outbound hop - it dies at startup before serving.

verdict.summary: A lowered 160m memory limit on fraud-detection causes the JVM to be killed for exceeding it, putting the service into a ~60s start-crash loop from 23:13 onward.
verdict.reasoning: The change log (tr_43452de6e2c1) shows platform-automation repeatedly lowering fraud-detection's memory limit to 160m and reverting it, with the last lowering at 23:13 and no revert before onset. The service's own logs (tr_c2ff4bd4f973) show nothing but JVM/agent startup banners repeating roughly every 60 seconds from ~23:16 through 23:21 - a process that starts and dies before doing work, consistent with being killed for exceeding the limit rather than failing requests. Error ratio barely moved (tr_650e9911080b) and many intervals had no defined value, i.e. no traffic, which fits a process that is absent rather than erroring. Traces (tr_ee372c0afd51) show only small, pre-onset, error-free work with no slow dependency hop, so waiting on a dependency is not the mechanism. flagd produced no logs and no changes (tr_992c218df220, tr_6704b1897443), so it is an idle member of the blast radius, not the cause. The limit edit is how it started; exhaustion of the memory it needed is what is happening.
open_questions: No container runtime OOM-kill record or memory-usage metric was inspected to confirm the kill reason directly.
Whether the 23:13 lowering was reverted after the observation window closed.
Why platform-automation repeatedly applies and reverts this limit.
